- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak heights.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent high or adjust downward 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive, model underreacts — increase forecast slope upward by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, add 0.3–0.5% daily drift toward historical mean.
- In absence of clear event context, model overweights recent sentiment — if sentiment is mixed or neutral, dampen forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term trend — if recent 10-day average is rising, forecast should trend upward by 0.1–0.2% per day beyond 10-day window.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
